subject: general
question: In the history of India, where did the Black Hole incident take place in the year 1756?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Black Hole of Calcutta was a small prison or dungeon in Fort William, Calcutta, where British soldiers and Indian sepoys were held by the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah.
 
• The incident took place on the night of June 20, 1756, when troops of Siraj-ud-Daulah captured Fort William.
 
• It is alleged that 146 prisoners were confined in a room measuring 14 by 18 feet, and by morning only 23 survived due to suffocation and heat exhaustion.
 
• The event was used by the British to justify their subsequent military actions in India, leading to the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daulah**

 
 
• Siraj-ud-Daulah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• He succeeded his grandfather, Alivardi Khan, in April 1756 and immediately faced challenges from the British East India Company.
 
• His attack on Fort William was a response to British military fortifications in Bengal without his permission.
 
• After his defeat at the Battle of Plassey, he was overthrown and executed.
 
 
 
• **Fort William**
 
 
• Fort William is a fort built in Calcutta in 1696 during the early years of British East India Company rule in India.
 
• The fort was named after King William III of England.
 
• It served as the British stronghold in Bengal and was the site of significant events in the early colonial history of India.
 
• After the Black Hole incident, the fort was extensively rebuilt and expanded.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Plassey**
 
 
• The Battle of Plassey was fought on June 23, 1757, between the forces of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah.
 
• It was a decisive victory for the British, largely due to the betrayal of Siraj-ud-Daulah's key general, Mir Jafar.
 
• The battle marked the beginning of British political control over India.
 
• It led to the establishment of the British East India Company's rule in Bengal and eventually all of India.
 
 

The correct answer is **Option 2**__.
